sections.title: Once and Future
sections.description: The medieval and the modernist touch across time in this experiment in trans period methods. We’ll look at what versions of the medieval interrupted, inspired, and were projected by late-nineteenth and early-twentieth-century writers. We’ll consider how the literary scholarship that sprang up around modernism informed and was informed by the study of medieval literature. And we’ll take up queerer, uncannier affiliations (through transhistorical desire, textual instability, and radical intertextuality) and attachments (to the fragment, the riddle, the macaronic). How do medievalists and modernists approach texts that all demand interpretation, (re)creation, and audience participation in meaning-making? Can we find a ‘modernist mode’ in the medieval, and vice versa? Readings will include medieval epic, elegy, romance, and whatever The Book of Margery Kempe is, along with the likes of Djuna Barnes, Samuel Beckett, David Jones, James Joyce, Virginia Woolf, and Miller Oberman.
